task.title: Users API
behaviours: POST /v1/users creates a user and returns 201 with a Location header pointing at /v1/users/{userId}; role defaults to member when omitted.
Creating a user whose email already exists returns 409 application/problem+json; so does changing a user's email (PATCH) to one another user already has.

GET /v1/users is cursor-paginated: query parameters limit (default 20, max 100) and cursor; the response is { data: User[], nextCursor: string | null } and following nextCursor visits every user exactly once.
GET, PATCH and DELETE on /v1/users/{userId} with an id that does not exist return 404 application/problem+json.
An invalid request body, query or path parameter returns 422 application/problem+json whose detail names each failing field; a malformed JSON body returns 400 application/problem+json.

POST /v1/users honours the Idempotency-Key header: repeating the same key with the same body replays the original response (Idempotent-Replayed: true) without creating a second user; reusing the key with a different body returns 422.
PATCH /v1/users/{userId} updates only the fields given and returns 200 with the updated user; an empty patch returns 422.
DELETE /v1/users/{userId} returns 204 with no body; the user is then gone (GET returns 404).

fields.name: email
fields.description: Login email address; unique across all users.

fields.name: role
fields.description: Access role; new users are members unless stated otherwise.
